interest: This document provides valuable historical evidence of pre-war tensions and diplomatic security measures in the months leading up to the Pearl Harbor attack. Dated August 1941, the entry reflects the Japanese government's attempt to survey assets held by first-generation Japanese residents (Issei) in Oregon, alongside emergency security preparations such as the destruction of consular correspondence in Portland. It highlights U.S. inter-agency surveillance of Japanese diplomatic and immigrant affairs during a critical geopolitical juncture marked by the resignation of the Japanese Cabinet.
overview: This file consists of a single Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheet (Form DS-46) dated October 12, 1945, cataloguing records under decimal classification 894.503111 relating to Japanese capital and investment in the United States. The sheet records a single communication (sub-number 2) dated August 14, 1941, originating from the Justice Department ('Notice Depart.'). The entry reports that the Japanese Foreign Office required a listing of property belonging to first-generation Japanese residents in Oregon, and notes intelligence regarding the resignation of the Japanese Cabinet and the burning of all correspondence at the Japanese Consulate in Portland, referencing cross-file 702.9411.

subfiles.about: A Department of State docket sheet recording document sub-number 2 concerning Japanese Foreign Office property registration requirements in Oregon and the destruction of consular records in Portland.
subfiles.summary: This Department of State List of Papers sheet (Form DS-46) dated October 12, 1945, indexes documents categorized under decimal file 894.503111 on Japanese capital in the United States. It summarizes an August 14, 1941 communication from the Justice Department reporting that the Japanese Foreign Office mandated the listing of property owned by first-generation Japanese (Issei) in Oregon. The entry further records intelligence advising of the resignation of the Japanese Cabinet and the burning of all correspondence in the Japanese Consul's office in Portland, with a cross-reference notation to file 702.9411.
